groupings.title: Git & GitHub
groupings.description: Worktrees, commits, pull requests, issues, releases, repo metadata, and workspace hygiene driven from the real diff and plan.

groupings.title: Writing & Docs
groupings.description: Make prose read like a person wrote it, and keep a project's in-repo contracts — reader documentation and the design system — true to the code.

groupings.title: Testing & QA
groupings.description: Review AI-written changes, prove a feature works, plan how to verify what you built, retrofit a real suite onto code that has none, and chase a symptom to its root cause when something breaks.

groupings.title: Planning & Design
groupings.description: Validate that an idea is worth building, research a technical decision, prototype your way to the answers reading won't settle, survey the code you already have for the structural change worth making, draft a plan from a rough idea, then pressure-test it before you write any code.

groupings.title: Building
groupings.description: Turn a hardened plan, spec, or issue into working code — straight-through or test-driven, gated on the repo's own tests and build — and make the UI half look like somebody chose it.

groupings.title: Skill & Prompt Authoring
groupings.description: Author the instructions an agent reads — new kit-convention skills from scratch, and the prompts you hand an agent or ship inside an application.

groupings.title: Context & Handoffs
groupings.description: Carry work across sessions and agents without losing the thread — the ubiquitous language, the decisions behind it, the state in flight, and where to pick up next.

groupings.title: Automation & Orchestration
groupings.description: Run the whole build span unattended — take a grilled, ready issue from worktree to open PR while you're away from the keyboard.

groupings.title: Thinking & Learning
groupings.description: Two personal repos that sit outside your work repos and get read one folder at a time — a folder per idea you're still thinking through, and a folder per subject you're learning, with spaced retrieval that comes back to check it stuck.
